author: lucaspbueno
body:
# 🚀 PR: Adição de ambiente Docker, collection do Postman e ajuste de exposição de detalhes de validação

## 📌 Descrição
Esta PR consolida melhorias importantes na estrutura e na experiência de uso da API, com foco em facilitar a execução local, padronizar testes manuais e tornar o comportamento de erros mais seguro em produção.

O principal objetivo foi adicionar suporte completo à execução via Docker, incluindo orquestração dos serviços necessários e execução automática das migrations no startup da aplicação. Além disso, foi incluída uma collection do Postman para apoiar o consumo e validação dos endpoints de CRUD de usuários, junto de ajustes nos placeholders das rotas. Por fim, também foi refinado o tratamento de erros de validação para que detalhes sensíveis sejam retornados apenas em ambiente de debug.

## 🔑 Alterações principais
- Adicionar configuração completa de Docker com `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose` e execução automática de `alembic upgrade head` no entrypoint
- Incluir collection do Postman para operações de CRUD de usuários e ajustar placeholders de `user_id` nas rotas
- Restringir o retorno de detalhes de erro `422 validation_error` apenas quando `DEBUG=true`, com atualização de testes e documentação

## ✅ Commits - Principais Commits
- `e39c7bb` build(docker): adicionar Dockerfile/compose e rodar alembic no entrypoint
- `cb722ba` docs(postman): adicionar collection do postman para CRUD de usuários
- `0c6c4d5` fix(exceptions): retornar detalhes de validação apenas em debug
- `56ea19d` fix(postman): ajustar placeholder de user_id nas rotas

## 📝 Observações
- A aplicação agora pode ser executada via Docker com os serviços `postgres`, `redis` e `api`
- O entrypoint executa `alembic upgrade head` antes de subir o `uvicorn`, então as migrations passam a fazer parte do fluxo de inicialização
- O comportamento do erro `422` muda conforme o ambiente: em produção (`DEBUG=false`), os detalhes de validação não são expostos
- O README foi atualizado com instruções de execução via Docker e referência à collection para testes manuais
- Houve ajuste no roteamento da API e remoção do endpoint de health anteriormente exposto

body:
Two bugs introduced by recent PRs caused 502 errors site-wide and a Turbopack build failure that prevented the frontend from starting at all. ## JSX syntax error (build failure) PR #289 placed `` as a sibling to the root `
` in the `return` of `app/suggestions/[id]/page.js` — invalid JSX (single root required). Turbopack rejected it with `Expected ',', got 'ident'` at line 443. ```jsx // before — two siblings at return root → parse error return (
...
// ← breaks build ); // after — wrapped in fragment return ( <>
...
); ``` ## Recurring 502s after `npm ci` (`start-frontend.js`) PR #287 bumped Next.js 16.1.6 → 16.2.0. After `npm ci`, the stale `.next` build causes `next start` to exit immediately; PM2 loops, nginx returns 502 for everything including `/` and `/favicon.ico`. New `start-frontend.js` (root-level, mirrors `deploy.sh`/`setup-db.sh` convention) gates startup on a freshness check: - Compares `mtime` of `node_modules/next/package.json` (bumped by `npm ci`) against `mtime` of `.next/BUILD_ID` (written at the end of `next build`). - If the build is absent or older than the installed package, runs `npm run frontend:build` automatically before handing off to `next start`. - Forwards `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT`/`SIGHUP` to the child process so PM2 and Docker shut down cleanly. `package.json` `frontend:start` updated from `next start -p 3001` → `node start-frontend.js`. The `deploy.sh` path (always explicit rebuild) is unchanged. ## Docs `doc/VPS_SETUP.md` and `doc/TROUBLESHOOTING.md` updated to reflect that `pm2 restart newsapp-frontend` is now safe after `npm ci` — the startup script handles the rebuild automatically. --- 💡 You can make Copilot smarter by setting up custom instructions, customizing its development environment and configuring Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. author: copilot
body:
Tapping the Usuario (client) dropdown in the garment search screen had no effect — the menu never opened. Root cause: `OutlinedTextField` consumes pointer events for focus handling, silently swallowing the `.clickable` modifier applied to it.

## Changes

- **`FilterDropdown` composable**: Removed `.clickable` from `OutlinedTextField`; added a transparent `Box` overlay with `.matchParentSize()` on top of the field to reliably intercept taps and expand the menu.
- Moved `DropdownMenu` inside an `items.isNotEmpty()` guard to prevent an empty popup from rendering on tap.

```kotlin
// Before — click consumed by TextField, dropdown never opens
OutlinedTextField(
    ...
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().clickable(enabled = enabled && items.isNotEmpty()) { expanded = true }
)

// After — transparent overlay intercepts the tap
OutlinedTextField(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), ...)
Box(modifier = Modifier.matchParentSize().clickable(enabled = items.isNotEmpty()) { expanded = true })
if (items.isNotEmpty()) { DropdownMenu(...) }
```

author: gfrmin
body:
## Summary

- **Bug**: When a user signs up with a purely non-Latin name (e.g. Chinese characters "邢佳兴"), Rails' `parameterize` strips all non-Latin characters and produces an empty string. FriendlyId then sets `url_name` to nil, causing a `PG::NotNullViolation` on the `users` table.
- **Fix**: After parameterizing the name, check if the result is blank and fall back to `'user'` — the same fallback already used for all-numeric names. The `sequentially_slugged` FriendlyId module automatically appends a numeric suffix (`user_2`, `user_3`, ...) to handle duplicate `'user'` slugs.
- This bug has been latent since FriendlyId was added to User in April 2023.

## Changes

- `app/models/user/slug.rb`: In `normalize_friendly_id`, store the parameterized result and return `super('user')` if it is blank.
- `spec/models/user_spec.rb`: Add a test for non-Latin names in the "making up the URL name" describe block.

## Test plan

- [ ] `bundle exec rspec spec/models/user_spec.rb` — new test passes, existing slug tests still green
- [ ] Manual test: create a user with a non-Latin name (e.g. "邢佳兴") and confirm signup succeeds with `url_name` set to `"user"`
- [ ] Create a second user with a non-Latin name and confirm `url_name` is `"user_2"` (sequential slug)

Vercel Web Analytics Implementation

Successfully configured Vercel Web Analytics for this plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript portfolio website.

## Changes Made

### Modified Files:
1. **index.html** - Added Vercel Analytics script tags in the <head> section
2. **thankyou.html** - Added Vercel Analytics script tags in the <head> section

### Implementation Details:

Following the official Vercel Analytics quickstart documentation (https://vercel.com/docs/analytics/quickstart), I implemented the plain HTML integration method which requires:

1. **Analytics initialization script** - Added before the closing </head> tag:
   ```javascript
   window.va = window.va || function () { (window.vaq = window.vaq || []).push(arguments); };
   ```

2. **Analytics loader script** - Added immediately after initialization:
   ```html
   <script defer src="/_vercel/insights/script.js"></script>
   ```

### Why This Approach:

- This is a **static HTML portfolio** (no build tools, no package.json)
- The project doesn't use npm, React, Next.js, or any JavaScript framework
- According to Vercel docs, plain HTML sites use the script-based integration (no npm package needed)
- The `/_vercel/insights/script.js` path is automatically served by Vercel when Analytics is enabled

### Next Steps to Complete Setup:

1. **Enable Analytics in Vercel Dashboard:**
   - Go to your project settings on Vercel
   - Navigate to the Analytics tab
   - Click "Enable Web Analytics"

2. **Deploy the changes:**
   - Push this branch to GitHub
   - Vercel will deploy with Analytics enabled

3. **Verify Installation:**
   - After deployment, open browser DevTools > Network tab
   - Visit your deployed site
   - Look for requests to `/_vercel/insights/*` endpoints
   - This confirms Analytics is tracking page views

### What Gets Tracked:

- Page views and unique visitors
- Page load performance metrics
- Referrer sources
- Device and browser information
- Geographic location (country-level)

All tracking is privacy-focused and GDPR-compliant by default.

author: lkosters
body:
## Summary
This PR significantly improves the Git panel UI and functionality by adding remote sync indicators, pull/fetch operations, file discard capability, and debounced refresh logic to prevent race conditions.

## Key Changes

**UI/UX Improvements:**
- Added sync status indicator showing ahead/behind commits relative to remote tracking branch
- Moved commit input to a persistent bar at the top of the actions section for better UX
- Added discard action (✕) to changed files, visible on hover alongside the stage (+) action
- Reorganized action buttons into separate "git-actions" and "git-sync-actions" bars

**New Git Operations:**
- Implemented `git:pull` command and pull button
- Implemented `git:fetch` command and fetch button
- Implemented `git:discard-file` command to discard changes in individual files

**Performance & Stability:**
- Added debounced refresh mechanism (`scheduleRefresh()`) with 100ms delay to prevent race conditions
- Refresh timer resets on manual refresh to avoid conflicts with polling
- Prevents multiple simultaneous refresh operations

**Code Quality:**
- Refactored `refreshGit()` to use debounced `scheduleRefresh()` internally
- Renamed internal refresh function to `doRefreshGit()` for clarity
- Improved event delegation for file actions (discard vs stage)
- Moved `data-stage` attribute from container to file name span for better semantics

**Backend Updates:**
- Extended git status response to include `ahead` and `behind` counts
- Calculates ahead/behind using `git rev-list --left-right --count` against tracking branch

## Implementation Details
- Commit input wrap now displays by default (not hidden) and visibility is controlled via CSS display property
- File action icons use color coding: green for stage (+), red for discard (✕)
- Sync status only displays when there are commits ahead or behind
- Debounce prevents excessive git operations during rapid UI interactions

### Description
- Added localization stack and simulation: `localization_error_model.py`, `localization_estimator.py`, `state_packet.py`, `anchor_provider.py`, and `uplink_delay_model.py` to simulate range perturbation, perform iterative least-squares 3D localization, represent localization packets, provide anchor geometry, and model uplink delays/queueing.

author: mherod
body:
## Problem

`gwork drive download <fileId> <destPath>` ignored the destination path argument and always saved to the current working directory using the original filename. Users had to manually move files afterwards.

## Fix

- Accept a positional destination argument (e.g. `gwork drive download <id> ~/Downloads/`)
- If the destination is an existing **directory**, append the original Drive filename inside it
- If the destination is a **file path**, write to that exact path
- Keep `--output <path>` flag for backwards compatibility
- Always fetch file metadata first to derive a safe filename for directory mode

## Usage (after fix)

```bash
# Save to a directory (auto-names using Drive filename)
gwork drive download 1abc ~/Downloads/assets/

# Save to an explicit file path
gwork drive download 1abc ~/Downloads/assets/my-photo.jpg

# --output flag still works
gwork drive download 1abc --output ~/Downloads/assets/my-photo.jpg
```

author: vivekghantiwala
body:
Fixes #1408

  ## What was wrong

  The `responsetime` condition check in `response_conditions_matched()`
  was using `exec()` to evaluate comparison operators pulled directly
  from YAML module configs. A crafted module file with something like
  `">= 0 or __import__('os').system('id')"` could get arbitrary Python
  executed during a scan.

  ## What I changed

  Replaced the `exec()` block with a simple operator dispatch dictionary
  that maps each valid operator string (`==`, `!=`, `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<`)
  to the corresponding `float` method. The behavior and supported operators
  are identical — just no more dynamic code execution.

  ## Files changed

  - `nettacker/core/lib/http.py` — replaced lines 76-91

## Description

Fixes race condition where frontend checks session before cookie is set.

### Problem

OAuth callback completes successfully on backend, but frontend request may hit
a race condition or stale session state during redirect, causing 500 error.
After refreshing the page, the session works correctly.

### Solution

Explicitly call configure_session(persist: true) after setting session values
to ensure the session cookie is properly saved before the response is sent
to the client.

### Changes

- Modified put_current_user/2 in UserAuth controller
- Added explicit session persistence to prevent race condition

- [x] This fix addresses the reported issue

author: davidberenstein1957
body:
## Overview

This PR automates the SDK to stay in sync with PrunaTree's canonical API definitions, eliminating manual drift and ensuring the provider works correctly with the latest Pruna API spec.

## What's Changed

### 🤖 Automated Codegen (scripts/codegen.js)
- Reads `P-API.json` and `model_param_defaults.json` from the PrunaTree submodule
- Auto-generates `PImageModelId` type union with all supported models
- Includes CI command: `npm run codegen:check` to prevent drift
- **Before**: Hardcoded model list prone to going out of sync
- **After**: Always matches the official spec

### 📊 Dynamic Schema-Driven Tests (src/p-image-schema.test.ts + schema-fixtures.ts)
- 26 comprehensive tests that validate:
  - Enum values (aspect_ratio, mode, etc.) match the spec
  - Required fields are documented correctly
  - Fields are properly isolated per model type
  - Default values are accurate
  - Schema structure is enforced (additionalProperties: false)
- Tests auto-expand as PrunaTree adds new models or fields
- Documents known gaps (p-image-lora missing from OpenAPI spec)

### ✨ SDK Improvements
1. **Added `mode` field** (from P-API.json)
   - Exposed on p-image-edit and p-image-edit-lora
   - 10 editing modes: default, relight, fusion, light_restoration, etc.
   - Properly warned when misused on generation models

2. **Fixed lora_scale default documentation**
   - Now correctly shows: 0.5 (generation) / 1 (edit-lora)
   - Sourced from model_param_defaults.json for accuracy

3. **TypeScript improvements**
   - Fixed schema-fixtures type casting
   - All tests handle models gracefully (even without OpenAPI schemas)

## Test Results

✅ **All 82 tests passing:**
- 56 SDK unit tests (existing + updated)
- 26 schema-driven tests (new)
- All tests validate against live PrunaTree definitions

✅ **Codegen verified:**
```bash
$ npm run codegen:check
✓ p-image-model.ts is up to date
```

## Known Discrepancies (Now Documented)

These gaps are documented in tests for future resolution:

1. **p-image-lora & p-image-edit-lora** exist in `model_param_defaults.json` but have no schemas in `P-API.json`
   - SDK still supports them (backend accepts them)
   - Tests note this gap for future spec update

2. **prompt_upsampling** field:
   - Present in defaults and SDK
   - NOT in P-API.json OpenAPI schema
   - Passed as undocumented field to API

3. **mode field** on p-image-edit:
   - Was completely missing from SDK
   - Now added and properly exposed

## Usage

```bash
# Regenerate SDK types from PrunaTree (use after updating submodule)
npm run codegen

# Verify SDK stays in sync (use in CI)
npm run codegen:check

# Run all tests
npm test

# Run only schema-driven tests
npm test -- p-image-schema.test.ts
```

## Files Changed

- `scripts/codegen.js` - Automated code generator (plain Node.js, no TypeScript runtime)
- `src/schema-fixtures.ts` - Test helper to load PrunaTree definitions
- `src/p-image-schema.test.ts` - Dynamic schema-driven test suite (26 tests)
- `src/p-image-model.ts` - Added mode field, fixed defaults, added codegen markers
- `package.json` - Added codegen and codegen:check scripts
- `.gitmodules` - PrunaTree submodule reference (already present)

## Future Work

- [ ] Extend codegen to auto-generate README defaults table
- [ ] Add support for all model types (not just image models)
- [ ] Consider exposing unknown fields (like mode) via a type-safe pass-through mechanism

## Related Issues

Fixes the issues where:
1. SDK hardcoded model fields instead of sourcing from spec
2. Tests were manual and didn't catch missing fields (like `mode`)
3. Defaults documentation diverged from actual backend defaults
4. No automated way to stay in sync with PrunaTree updates

---

## 概要

LSP 機能（tsgo + Vue Language Server の起動・診断通知）を一時的に無効化する。

## 背景

現時点で LSP 診断パネルを積極的に使用していないため、不要なプロセス起動を避ける。将来的に再有効化する可能性があるため、コード削除ではなくフラグによる無効化とした。

## 変更内容

### desktop

- `rendererReady` 内の LSP 起動ブロックを `if (lspEnabled)` で囲み、`lspEnabled = false` で無効化
- 再有効化時はフラグを `true` に変更するだけで復帰可能

### 変更なし

- renderer 側の diagnostics コード（store, パネル, RPC 購読）はメッセージが来なければ空のまま動作するため変更不要
- RPC スキーマの `lspDiagnostics` メッセージ定義もそのまま残す

## スコープ

- **スコープ内**: LSP 起動の無効化
- **スコープ外（対応しない）**: LSP 関連コード・依存パッケージの削除（再有効化の可能性があるため）

body:
## Milestone 2: Memory Pipeline

Implements the complete memory pipeline — LLM text generation, fact extraction,
memory evolution, and the MemoryManager orchestrator. All three Milestone 2
issues are complete.

---

### Issues Closed

**#6 — Implement fact extraction pipeline**
- `AbstractLLMService` ABC with `complete()` and `complete_with_tool()` methods
- `LLMError` for clean failure propagation
- `ClaudeService` backed by `AsyncAnthropic` with forced `tool_choice`
  to guarantee structured output
- `ExtractionPipeline` loads system prompt from `extraction.txt` at runtime,
  calls `extract_facts` tool to extract candidate facts from a `ConversationPair`
- `_build_user_content` assembles conversation summary + recent messages +
  current pair into a single structured prompt
- Defensive `isinstance` check and `str` coercion on LLM output

**#7 — Implement memory evolution engine**
- `EvolutionEngine.decide()` takes a candidate fact + pre-retrieved memories
- `_DECIDE_OPERATION_TOOL` schema enforces `ADD`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`/`NOOP`
- `_parse_result` falls back to `NOOP` on invalid or incomplete LLM output
- Guards for missing `memory_id` on `UPDATE`/`DELETE`, missing
  `updated_content` on `UPDATE` — prevents silent data corruption
- `_build_user_content` formats candidate fact + existing memories for LLM

**#8 — Build MemoryManager orchestrator**
- `MemoryManager` is the single public entry point for the memory service
- `add_memory`: extract candidates → embed each → search similar →
  evolve → persist `ADD`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`/`NOOP`
- `UPDATE` re-embeds `updated_content` (not the candidate) to keep
  embedding and content aligned for future similarity search
- `search_memory`: embed query → store search → return ranked results
- Graceful skip when `UPDATE` targets a non-existent memory

---

### Tests
73 behavioral tests across 6 packages — all passing.
Google-style: test behavior not implementation, one reason to fail per test,
no mocking except external I/O, no cross-service imports in test files.

---

### Dependency Graph (completed layers)
```
config
  └── storage
        └── llm
              └── memory  ← Milestone 2 complete
```
`retrieval → api` to follow in Milestone 3.

---

Closes #6
Closes #7
Closes #8

body:
#### Context

Issue `#113` needs a way to keep Symphony from assigning work immediately on startup and to let an operator pause or resume new assignment without interrupting work already in flight.

#### TL;DR

Add config-backed start/stop orchestration controls in the host UI and API.

#### Summary

- add an orchestrator control service with `Started` / `Stopped` state and config-backed initial startup behavior
- gate polling, queued dispatch, and retry dispatch so stopping blocks new assignment while in-flight work continues
- expose orchestration state plus start/stop actions through the API and sidebar shell, and document the new config

#### Alternatives

- gate only the polling loop, but that would still allow queued or retry work to start while the UI said the orchestrator was stopped
- add UI-only controls without API/state plumbing, but that would make the host harder to automate and test

## Summary

Move identified flaky tests to a non-blocking suite.

This PR introduces a mechanism to skip flaky integration tests by default, using a `skipFlaky` constant in the integration test helper. It also moves several identified flaky tests to this non-blocking suite.

- **Integration Test Suite**: Added a `skipFlaky` constant in `integration-tests/test-helper.ts` that is `true` unless `RUN_FLAKY_INTEGRATION=1` is set.

body:
A browser-only tool for commercial glazing professionals: upload tender PDFs → extract window/door schedule data → review/edit → generate a professional quote PDF. Zero server, zero API keys.

## Architecture

7 focused ES5-compatible JS modules loaded as plain `<script>` tags — no build step required:

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `pdfParser.js` | PDF.js drag-drop + text extraction with per-page progress |
| `dataExtractor.js` | Regex pattern engine: item refs (`W01`, `D02`…), dimensions, frame types, glazing specs, opening types, special notes; cross-document discrepancy detection |
| `dataModel.js` | Central state, `localStorage` persistence, JSON import/export, prototype-pollution-safe `deepMerge` |
| `pricing.js` | per-m² base rate × frame/opening/glazing/special multipliers + VAT + discount |
| `ui.js` | Sortable/filterable inline-editable table, confidence badges, warnings panel, dark mode |
| `quoteGenerator.js` | jsPDF A4 output: navy header, itemised schedule grouped by type, price summary, T&Cs |
| `app.js` | Orchestration, 30s auto-save, modal/toast system |

## Key behaviours

- **Confidence scoring** — every extracted item is rated `high`/`medium`/`low` based on how many fields were resolved (ref, both dimensions, frame type, location)
- **Cross-document validation** — flags items present in one doc but missing from another, and dimension/qty mismatches between documents
- **Graceful degradation** — scanned/image PDFs trigger a warning; all fields remain manually editable; extraction errors never crash the app
- **Pricing overrides** — per-item `manualOverride` flag prevents global rate changes from clobbering user-set prices
- **Session persistence** — full state round-trips through `localStorage` and JSON export/import

## CDN dependencies

```html
<!-- All scripts pinned with SRI hashes -->

  integrity="sha512-..." crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/jspdf/2.5.1/jspdf.umd.min.js"
  integrity="sha512-..." crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

  integrity="sha512-..." crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
```

<summary>Original prompt</summary>


## Overview

Build a complete **Glazing Quote Assistant** web application that runs entirely client-side and can be hosted on **GitHub Pages**. This is a tool for commercial glazing professionals that reads tender pack PDFs, extracts window/door schedule data, lets the user review and edit everything, and then generates a professional quote PDF.

The existing repo has:
- A blank `README.md`
- `Tender docs/` — real tender pack PDFs from a commercial glazing job (Berryfields Farm Hotel project):
  - `3847.T05 Proposed Ground Floor Plan.pdf`
  - `3847.T06 Proposed First Floor Plan.pdf`
  - `3847.T07 Proposed Elevations.pdf`
  - `3847.T12 Window Schedule.pdf`
  - `BQ pages Windows & Doors.pdf`
  - `Collateral Warranties & Guarantees.pdf`
  - `ENQUIRY LETTER.pdf`
  - `New docs sent by Phil 14-03-2025/` (email + zip with additional docs)
- `quote/` — example finished quote PDFs:
  - `Berryfields - Fenster Glazing Quote (2).pdf` (windows quote)
  - `Berryfields Doors - Fenster Glazing Quote.pdf` (doors quote)

These documents serve as reference for what kind of data gets extracted and what the final output should roughly look like.

## Architecture & Technical Requirements

### Must be GitHub Pages compatible
- **100% client-side** — no server, no backend, no API keys required to run
- Static HTML/CSS/JS (can use a build step if needed, but keep it simple)
- PDF parsing must happen in the browser using libraries like **PDF.js** (for text extraction) and **pdf-lib** or **jsPDF** (for PDF generation)

### Project Structure
Organize into clean, modular directories:
```
/
├── index.html              # Main entry point
├── css/
│   └── styles.css          # All styling
├── js/
│   ├── app.js              # Main application controller / orchestration
│   ├── pdfParser.js         # PDF upload handling + text extraction (PDF.js)
│   ├── dataExtractor.js     # NLP/regex logic to find windows, doors, sizes, quantities, notes
│   ├── dataModel.js         # Data structures, state management, validation
│   ├── ui.js                # DOM rendering, table building, user interactions
│   ├── pricing.js           # Pricing engine (flexible, override-friendly)
│   └── quoteGenerator.js    # Final quote PDF generation
├── lib/                     # Third-party libraries (PDF.js, jsPDF/pdf-lib, etc.)
├── assets/                  # Logo placeholder, icons, fonts
├── Tender docs/             # (existing) reference documents - keep as-is
├── quote/                   # (existing) example quotes - keep as-is
└── README.md                # Updated with project documentation
```

## Feature Requirements

### 1. PDF Upload & Parsing (`pdfParser.js`)
- Drag-and-drop zone + file picker for multiple PDFs
- Show upload progress and file list
- Use **PDF.js** to extract text content from each page of each PDF
- Handle large files gracefully (show progress, don't freeze the UI)
- Support common PDF issues (scanned-image PDFs should show a warning that text extraction may fail)

### 2. Data Extraction (`dataExtractor.js`)
- After text extraction, run pattern-matching logic to identify:
  - **Item references** (e.g., W01, W02, D01, D02, etc.)
  - **Item types** (window, door, screen, curtain wall, etc.)
  - **Dimensions** — width × height in mm
  - **Quantities**
  - **Special notes** — fire rated, acoustic, toughened, laminated, trickle vents, restrictors, etc.
  - **Location/floor** — ground floor, first floor, etc.
  - **Frame material** — aluminium, PVCu, timber, etc.
  - **Glazing spec** — double glazed, triple glazed, obscure, clear, etc.
  - **Opening type** — fixed, casement, top-hung, tilt-and-turn, sliding, etc.
- For each extracted item, include a **confidence indicator**:
  - ✅ High confidence — clear match
  - ⚠️ Medium — partial match or inferred
  - ❓ Low — guessed or conflicting data
- Cross-reference data between documents (e.g., the window schedule should match items in the BQ)
- Flag discrepancies (e.g., schedule says 10 windows but BQ says 8)
- Create a summary of what was found vs what might be missing

### 3. Data Model (`dataModel.js`)
- Central state object holding all extracted line items
- Each item should have this shape (at minimum):
```javascript
{
  id: "uuid",
  reference: "W01",           // Item reference from documen

body:
## Why

When the CLI process uses a lot of memory, users have no way to know about it or what to do. They only find out when their system slows down or the process gets killed.

## What changed

The TUI sidebar now shows a "Memory" section when the process uses more than 2 GB of RAM. It displays total memory in a warning color alongside what's currently active — connected MCP servers, plugins, and messages in the session — so users can understand what's contributing. It also suggests running `/compact` or `/new` to free memory. The server exposes a lightweight memory endpoint, and the TUI polls it every 10 seconds with negligible overhead since it runs in-process.

## How to test

1. Start the CLI with `bun run dev` and open a session
2. The Memory section should not appear (RSS is below 2 GB in normal use)
3. To verify it works, temporarily lower the threshold in `sidebar.tsx` from `2 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024` to something small like `1`
4. Confirm the sidebar shows "Memory" with the current GB value, active counts, and the `/compact or /new` tip
5. Restore the original threshold

Generator scripts had `.lua` extensions (ModuleScript in Rojo), so they never auto-ran on server start. RemoteEvents were scattered across top-level ReplicatedStorage and ad-hoc subfolders (`Events/`, `Race/`), and the Rojo StarterPlayer config triggered bug #1154 (delete warnings on every sync).

## Structural fixes

- **Generator extensions** — renamed `Generate*.lua` → `Generate*.server.lua` so Rojo creates Scripts that auto-run; removed `--[[ TEMPORARILY DISABLED ]]` wrappers from Mountain/RaceTrack generators (replaced by `Disabled: true` in `.meta.json`)
- **Deleted dead code** — `StarterGui/ShopGui_d/`, `StarterPlayerScripts/Client/` (superseded by `PaintShopButton.client.lua`); root-level duplicate generator files
- **StarterPlayer Rojo fix** — replaced `"$path": "src/StarterPlayer"` with explicit `$className` children for both `StarterPlayerScripts` and `StarterCharacterScripts`, each with `$ignoreUnknownInstances: true`

## ReplicatedStorage reorganization

- **`Module/` → `Shared/`** — all four data modules moved; all `require()` paths updated across every script
- **`Remotes.model.json`** — single `Folder` declaring all 19 `RemoteEvent`s; replaces inline definitions scattered across `default.project.json` (`OpenPaintShop`, `Events/OpenGarage`, `Events/EquipVehicle`, `Race/*`, etc.)

```lua
-- Before (fragmented across 3 locations)
local raceFolder        = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Race", 10)
local eventsFolder      = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Events", 10)
local openPaintShop     = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("OpenPaintShop")

-- After (single Remotes folder)
local remotesFolder     = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Remotes", 10)
local checkpointReached = remotesFolder:WaitForChild("CheckpointReached", 10)
local openGarage        = remotesFolder:WaitForChild("OpenGarage", 10)
```

## ServerScriptService reorganization

- `Services/` — all six handler scripts (`CheckpointHandler`, `CoinHandler`, `GarageHandler`, `PaintShopHandler`, `TimerHandler`, and renamed `MapSelector` → `MapSelectHandler`)
- `Setup/` — three generator scripts + two `.meta.json` disable files
- `$ignoreUnknownInstances: true` added to all service entries in `default.project.json`

author: shuklaayush
body:
### Summary
Redesign `keccakf_perm_tracegen` as a two-phase kernel to fix a memory coalescing bottleneck. The original single-kernel design assigned 24 consecutive rows per thread, causing adjacent warp threads to store 24 rows apart in the column-major trace — wasting ~97% of memory bandwidth. The new design separates state computation (thread-per-permutation) from trace writing (thread-per-row), so adjacent threads write adjacent rows and stores coalesce. **~58x kernel speedup** (9.2s → 160ms total GPU time across 138 invocations on the reth benchmark).

### Changes

**`p3_keccakf.cuh`:**
- Add `apply_round_in_place`: keccak-f round function (theta/rho/pi/chi/iota) without trace column writes, used by phase 1
- Add `RHO_PI_CYCLE_IDX`/`RHO_PI_CYCLE_ROT` constants for in-place rho/pi permutation cycle
- `generate_trace_row_for_round`: replace `state_b[5][5]` with in-place rho/pi, replace `state_c_prime[5]` with scalar `d`, in-place chi with 2 temps per row

**`keccakf_perm.cu`:**
- Phase 1 kernel (`keccakf_perm_phase1`): one thread per permutation computes all 24 keccak-f rounds, stores 25-lane u64 round-input state to a scratch buffer (~4.8 KB/permutation)
- Phase 2 kernel (`keccakf_perm_phase2`): one thread per row loads round state from scratch, writes all 2634 trace columns with coalesced stores
- Remove `initial_state[5][5]`, `fill_zero`, and prev-row global readback
- Unify valid/dummy code paths (dummy rows use zero-initialized state)

**`cuda_abi.rs` / `mod.rs`:**
- Plumb scratch buffer (`DeviceBuffer<u64>`) through FFI to the CUDA kernels
- Scratch overhead is ~1.9% of the trace matrix (4800 bytes/perm for scratch vs 252864 bytes/perm for the trace), freed after tracegen completes

[Reth benchmark comparison](https://github.com/axiom-crypto/openvm-eth/actions/runs/23360309931)

Resolves INT-6958

author: balzaniedoardo
body:
Closes #486

## Summary

- Introduces `CategoryBasis` / `Category`, a new basis class for one-hot encoding categorical variables.
- Generalizes the bounds guard from `CategoryBasis` to `BasisMixin` via `_is_discrete`, so any future discrete basis gets the behaviour automatically.
- Adds a comprehensive test suite covering all public API paths of `CategoryBasis`, plus a new `TestDiscreteBasis` class parametrized over all `_is_discrete` classes.

## Motivation

Discrete task variables (trial type, stimulus identity, neuron id) are common in neuroscience GLMs but had no first-class support in NeMoS. Users had to manually one-hot encode outside the pipeline, breaking the `compute_features` / `sklearn` integration. `CategoryBasis` fills this gap while fitting naturally into the existing basis composition framework (issue #486).

## Description of the Changes and Rationale

### New class: `CategoryBasis` / `Category` (`src/nemos/basis/_category.py`)

| Feature | Detail |
|---|---|
| `categories` | Accepts `int`, `list`, `NDArray`, or JAX array; stored sorted; `n_basis_funcs` updates on re-assignment |
| `out_of_category` | `bool`; if `True`, unknown labels encode as all-zero rows; if `False`, raises `ValueError` on unknown labels |
| JIT | Supported only when `out_of_category=True`; raises a clear `ValueError` under `jax.jit` otherwise (see rationale below) |
| `evaluate_on_grid` | Raises `NotImplementedError` — method is meaningless for discrete inputs |
| `_is_discrete = True` | Marks the class as discrete; used by `BasisMixin` to guard bounds access |

**JIT compatibility.** When `out_of_category=False`, `evaluate` must inspect the concrete values of the input array to detect unknown labels and raise. Under `jax.jit`, arrays are abstract tracers — their values are unavailable at trace time — making this check impossible. `out_of_category=True` sidesteps the issue by replacing unknown labels with `-1` via `jnp.where` / `np.isin`, which are JAX-traceable operations that never require concrete values.

**`_set_out_of_category` dtype dispatch.** The method dispatches across three dtype paths to correctly identify out-of-category labels regardless of whether categories and inputs are numeric or string-typed.

### Bounds guard generalized to `BasisMixin` (`src/nemos/basis/_basis_mixin.py`)

`__getattr__` and `__setattr__` overrides were moved from `CategoryBasis` to `BasisMixin`, conditioned on `self._is_discrete`. The error message uses `self.__class__.__name__` so it remains informative for any future discrete subclass. The guard intentionally accesses `_is_discrete` directly (no `getattr` fallback) so that a basis missing the `BasisMixin` contract fails loudly.

## Questions
- The adding one or more categorical predictors creates perfect linear dependencies in the design matrix rows. Adding regularizers can make the problem identifiable, however, the identifiability problem is very nuanced. I added a long detail note as part of the docstrings, but in the how-to-guide I focused on simple operational recommendations. Is this the best way to present the issue to the user? Is the note in the docstrings visible enough?
- Currently we implement a very simple dummy coding, I think this is what our basis should provide, any more complex coding requires a careful algorithmic implementation. I think we should point to `patsy` or `formulaic` for more complex scenarios. Does this make sense?
- Should we support a `pynapple` compatible formula based design? `nmo.from_formula("x+y+x:y", tsdframe)`, so that people can drop pynaple directly. This basically just wraps `patsy` or `formulaic`?

author: copilot
body:
The DLQ error message in `handle_dlq_response` used Ruby's `to_s` on hashes, which changed format between JRuby 9 (`"key"=>"value"`) and JRuby 10 (`"key": "value"`), causing brittle regex-based test assertions.

## Changes

- **`lib/logstash/plugin_mixins/elasticsearch/common.rb`**: Replace string interpolation of `action_params` and `response` with `LogStash::Json.dump(...)`, producing stable JSON output across JRuby versions:
  ```ruby
  # Before
  detailed_message = "#{message} status: #{status}, action: #{action_params}, response: #{response}"
  # After
  detailed_message = "#{message} status: #{status}, action: #{LogStash::Json.dump(action_params)}, response: #{LogStash::Json.dump(response)}"
  ```

- **`spec/unit/outputs/elasticsearch_spec.rb`**: Replace the version-sensitive regex with straightforward `include` assertions on JSON key-value pairs:
  ```ruby
  # Before — fragile, handles JRuby 9/10 differences
  expect(reason).to match /_id(?::| ?=>) ?"bar".*"foo" ?=> ?"bar".*response:.*"reason" ?=> ?"TEST"/
  # After — simple, format-agnostic
  expect(reason).to include '"_id":"bar"'
  expect(reason).to include '"foo":"bar"'
  expect(reason).to include '"reason":"TEST"'
  ```

## Summary

Closes #139

Replaces the free-text `paymentDetails` field with structured payment method types that support deep links to open payment apps directly.

## Changes

### Data Model
- Added `paymentMethods` JSON column to `EventCost` (migration `20260320120000`)
- Format: `[{ type: "mbway"|"revolut_tag"|"revolut_link"|"phone", value: "...", label?: "..." }]`
- Legacy `paymentDetails` field kept for backward compatibility

### Shared Library (`src/lib/paymentMethods.ts`)
- Type definitions for 4 payment method types
- Validation (phone digit count, Revolut tag format, revolut.me/rev.money URL domains)
- Normalization (strip `@` from tags, remove spaces from phone numbers)
- Deep link generation:
  - **Phone**: `tel:+number`
  - **MB Way**: no public deep link — copy fallback with instructions
  - **Revolut Tag**: `https://revolut.me/<user>?amount=X&currency=Y`
  - **Revolut Link**: direct URL passthrough

### API (`cost.ts` PUT)
- Accepts optional `paymentMethods` array in request body
- Validates and normalizes before persisting as JSON
- Supports clearing (`null` or `[]`), preserves when omitted

### UI (`PaymentSection.tsx`)
- **Edit mode**: Structured form with type selector + value input per method, "Add payment method" button, legacy free-text field still available
- **Read mode**: Each method rendered as a card with branded icon, deep link button (opens app), and copy button. MB Way shows copy + instructions. Legacy `paymentDetails` shown as fallback when no structured methods exist.

### i18n
- 13 new keys added to all 6 locales (en, pt, es, fr, de, it)

### Tests
- 28 unit tests for `paymentMethods.ts` (validation, normalization, deep links, parsing)
- 11 integration tests for the API (save, retrieve, validation errors, clearing, backward compat, recurrence reset persistence)
- All 604 tests pass

author: claude
body:
macOS emits spurious `MallocStackLogging: can't turn off malloc stack logging because it was not enabled` warnings when spawning Python subprocesses without explicitly setting the malloc stack logging state.

## Changes

- Set `MallocStackLogging=0` in subprocess environment when spawning MLX Whisper worker process (processor.py:1399-1401)

```python
# Before
proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, bufsize=1)

# After  
env = os.environ.copy()
env['MallocStackLogging'] = '0'
proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, bufsize=1, env=env)
```

This eliminates console noise during batch translation operations on macOS.

- The status filter and button are grouped together, ensuring they stay aligned on larger screens

body:
### Motivation
- Make editor behavior explicit when a user starts editing a prompt that was displayed as an English fallback (`en_fallback`) so the editor stops mutating the model EN prompt indefinitely and the edited text becomes the primary (RU) working prompt.

### Description
- On first edit while `imagePromptEditorLang`/`videoPromptEditorLang` is `en_fallback`, the handler now promotes the edited text into `imagePromptRu`/`videoPromptRu`, switches the editor lang to `ru`, clears the live model EN fields, and preserves the original EN fallback in `imagePromptEnSource`/`videoPromptEnSource` instead of overwriting `imagePromptEn`/`videoPromptEn`.
- The change updates prompt presence/status fields accordingly (`enPromptPresent`, `ruPromptMissing`, `promptLanguageStatus`) and triggers a prompt re-sync via `scheduleComfyPromptSync` for the promoted RU text.
- The UI keeps the existing fallback-display logic but now surfaces the preserved original EN fallback source below the editor so the original source is visible after promotion.
- Changes are implemented in `frontend/src/pages/ClipStoryboardPage.jsx` (image and video prompt change handlers and the related UI blocks).

### Testing
- Built the frontend with `npm run build`, and the build completed successfully.

body:
# Tổng quan

Pull Request này tập trung vào chuẩn hóa định dạng tiền tệ trên toàn bộ hệ thống e-learning marketplace. Thay vì để các component view tự định dạng tiền tệ bằng JSTL tag (`fmt:formatNumber`) hoặc JavaScript, toàn bộ logic định dạng tiền tệ được tập trung vào một utility class duy nhất. Điều này đảm bảo tính nhất quán khi hiển thị giá tiền, hỗ trợ đa region (VND/USD), và giúp hệ thống dễ bảo trì hơn khi thay đổi chính sách định dạng.

---

# Các thay đổi chính

## 1. Tạo utility class định dạng tiền tệ

- Tạo mới class **DataFormatting** để centralize toàn bộ logic định dạng tiền tệ  
- Method chính: `formatAndConvert(double priceInVND)`  
  - Định dạng và quy đổi tiền tệ theo locale/region người dùng  
- Hỗ trợ:
  - VND mặc định  
  - USD (quy đổi bằng cách chia cho 25,000 khi region = "US")  
- Sử dụng `NumberFormat` của Java để đảm bảo chuẩn quốc tế theo locale  

---

## 2. Cập nhật DTO / Model classes

Thêm các method getter để trả về dữ liệu đã được format sẵn:

- **CourseCardDto**
  - `getOriginPrice()`
  - `getDiscountedPrice()`

- **CourseDetailDto**
  - Tương tự CourseCardDto

- **CartItem**
  - `getPriceFormat()`

- **OrderDTO**
  - `getFormatFinal()`

- **OrderItemDTO**
  - `getPriceAtPurchaseFormat()`

---

## 3. Cập nhật Service Cart

- Mở rộng `CartService`:
  - `getFormatedTotal()`
  - `getFormatedFinalPriceTotal()`
  - `getFormatedDiscountPriceTotal()`

- `CartServiceImpl`:
  - Implement các method mới  
  - Sử dụng `DataFormatting.formatAndConvert()` để xử lý toàn bộ logic tiền tệ  

---

## 4. Cập nhật Controller Cart

- `CartManagerController`
- `UpdateSelectController`

Thay đổi response JSON:

- Trả về `finalPriceTotal`, `total` đã được format sẵn  
- Không còn trả dữ liệu số thô cho client xử lý  

---

## 5. Cập nhật View Pages

Thay thế toàn bộ `fmt:formatNumber` bằng EL expression từ model:

### Trang chủ (index.jsp)
- `${courseMostPopular.discountedPrice}`
- `${courseMostPopular.originPrice}`
- `${c.discountedPrice}`
- `${c.originPrice}`

### Giỏ hàng (cart.jsp)
- Giá từng item
- Tổng tiền thanh toán

### Payment (payment.jsp)
- Giá khóa học trong order
- Tổng giá gốc
- Số tiền giảm
- Tổng thanh toán

### Receipt (receipt.jsp)
- Hiển thị hóa đơn sau thanh toán

### All Course (all-course.jsp)
- Thay toàn bộ `fmt:formatNumber`

### Course Detail (course-detail.jsp)
- Cập nhật hiển thị giá

### Search (result-search.jsp)
- Giá trong danh sách kết quả

### Wishlist (my-wishlist.jsp)
- Giá khóa học yêu thích

### Order History (order-history.jsp)
- Tổng tiền đơn hàng

---

## 6. Cập nhật JavaScript

- `cart-action.js`:
  - Loại bỏ `Intl.NumberFormat`
  - Không còn xử lý format tiền ở client  
  - Vì server đã trả dữ liệu đã format  

---

## 7. Tái cấu trúc JSP layout

- Di chuyển `toast.jsp`:
  - Từ `views/layouts/`
  - → `views/components/`

- Cập nhật toàn bộ reference tại:
  - category-management.jsp  
  - course-create.jsp  
  - courses-management.jsp  
  - lesson-management.jsp  
  - order-create.jsp  
  - payment-method-management.jsp  
  - tag-management.jsp  
  - users-management.jsp  
  - payment.jsp  

---

# Chi tiết kỹ thuật

## Centralized Formatting Logic

- Toàn bộ format tiền tệ xử lý tại server:
  - `DataFormatting.formatAndConvert()`
- Loại bỏ inconsistency giữa:
  - JSP JSTL
  - JavaScript
  - Backend logic  

---

## Locale-aware Formatting

- Sử dụng:
  - `NumberFormat.getCurrencyInstance(locale)`
- Đảm bảo:
  - Format đúng theo vùng người dùng  

---

## Regional Currency Conversion

- Hỗ trợ tự động:
  - VND (mặc định)
  - USD (region = "US")
- Quy đổi:
  - 1 USD = 25,000 VND  

---

## View Simplification

- EL expression thay thế JSTL formatting
- Code JSP gọn hơn
- Dễ đọc và dễ maintain hơn  

---

## AJAX Optimization

- Cart API trả về:
  - giá đã format sẵn
- Giảm xử lý phía client
- Giảm phụ thuộc JS formatting logic  

---

# Kết quả đạt được

- Tính nhất quán cao: toàn hệ thống hiển thị cùng một chuẩn tiền tệ  
- Dễ bảo trì: chỉ cần sửa `DataFormatting` khi thay đổi format  
- Hỗ trợ đa region tốt hơn (VND / USD)  
- Giảm logic frontend, tăng hiệu năng và đơn giản hóa JS  
- UI hiển thị giá tiền chuyên nghiệp và đồng bộ hơn

| D9-005 | Erase malformed `peer_payload` from NVS | `node-requirements.md` ND-0910 criterion 3 |
| D9-006 | `GET_CHUNK` retries use fresh sequence numbers | `protocol.md` section 9.2 |
| D9-007 | Ephemeral programs with maps rejected | `node-requirements.md` ND-0503 criterion 4 |

body:
This pull request updates the logic for generating anchor slugs and table of contents (TOC) slugs in the changelog directive to ensure they consistently match the heading IDs produced by the renderer. This improves navigation accuracy, especially for version headings and section links in the right-hand navigation. The changes also update the corresponding test to reflect the new slug format.

Slug consistency improvements:

* Updated `ComputeGeneratedAnchors()` and `ComputeTableOfContent()` in `ChangelogBlock.cs` to use a new `anchorSlug` (created by applying `.Slugify()` to the title slug) for all section anchors, ensuring consistency between generated anchors and heading IDs. This affects all section links such as "breaking changes", "security", etc. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ec89035fc45dfc832e4a3e38cb05c811df2cce53e4a5fe321a5b0c5d2dbb1b5cR312) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ec89035fc45dfc832e4a3e38cb05c811df2cce53e4a5fe321a5b0c5d2dbb1b5cL321-R354) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-ec89035fc45dfc832e4a3e38cb05c811df2cce53e4a5fe321a5b0c5d2dbb1b5cL417-R424) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-ec89035fc45dfc832e4a3e38cb05c811df2cce53e4a5fe321a5b0c5d2dbb1b5cL427-R434) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-ec89035fc45dfc832e4a3e38cb05c811df2cce53e4a5fe321a5b0c5d2dbb1b5cL439-R462) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-ec89035fc45dfc832e4a3e38cb05c811df2cce53e4a5fe321a5b0c5d2dbb1b5cL466-R473) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-ec89035fc45dfc832e4a3e38cb05c811df2cce53e4a5fe321a5b0c5d2dbb1b5cL475-R482) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-ec89035fc45dfc832e4a3e38cb05c811df2cce53e4a5fe321a5b0c5d2dbb1b5cL484-R491) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-ec89035fc45dfc832e4a3e38cb05c811df2cce53e4a5fe321a5b0c5d2dbb1b5cL493-R500) [[10]](diffhunk://#diff-ec89035fc45dfc832e4a3e38cb05c811df2cce53e4a5fe321a5b0c5d2dbb1b5cL502-R509)
* Changed the TOC version header slug to use the display version's `.Slugify()` instead of the raw title slug, so that TOC links scroll to the correct section (e.g., "November 2025" becomes "november-2025").

Testing updates:

* Updated the test `TocSlugMatchesHeadingId` in `ChangelogVersionSortingTests.cs` to check for the new slug format (e.g., "december-2025" instead of "2025-12").

Dependency update:

* Added a `using Elastic.Markdown.Helpers;` directive to `ChangelogBlock.cs` to enable use of the `.Slugify()` extension method.

author: sawicki-maciej
body:
## Summary

Remove inline manifest content hashes from `reinstall_trigger` to prevent Renovate dependency bumps from triggering full server reinstalls.

## Related Issue
Fixes #205

## Root Cause

`terraform_data.reinstall_trigger` tracked `sha256(local.cluster_config_patch)`, which includes the rendered content of Cilium install Job and ZFS pool Job templates. When Renovate bumps a provider version, the templates may render differently (e.g., different image digests), changing the hash and triggering a reinstall — wiping disk, etcd, and ZFS pools.

## Fix

**Removed from trigger:**
- `sha256(local.cluster_config_patch)` — contains inline manifest content that changes with dependency updates

**Added to trigger (boot-critical):**
- `sha256(local.extra_host_entries_config_patch)` — host DNS entries
- `var.zfs_pool_enabled` — structural toggle

**Already tracked (unchanged):**
- Image URL, version, type, EFI path
- Cluster name, endpoint
- Extensions, Tailscale config, firewall CIDRs
- ZFS config patch, ephemeral volume patch

## Trade-off

Inline manifests are baked into the config drive, so changing them technically requires a reinstall OR `talosctl apply-config`. However, since these manifests run as Kubernetes Jobs that execute once after boot, the existing Jobs will have already completed. New manifest content only takes effect on the next reinstall anyway.

## Impact

- **One-time**: This PR will trigger a reinstall (changing the trigger list changes its ID)
- **Going forward**: Renovate merges will NOT trigger reinstalls

## Testing
- [x] `tofu validate` passes

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary by Sourcery

Adjust reinstall trigger inputs to avoid unnecessary full server reinstalls on dependency updates.

Bug Fixes:
- Stop Renovate-driven dependency changes from triggering full server reinstalls by excluding inline manifest content from the reinstall trigger.

Enhancements:
- Refine reinstall trigger to track only machine-level and structural configuration changes, including extra host entries and ZFS pool enablement toggle.

author: richm
body:
The role gathers the facts it uses.  For example, if the user uses
`ANSIBLE_GATHERING=explicit`, the role uses the `setup` module with the
facts and subsets it requires.

This change allows us to test this.  Before every role invocation, the test
will use `meta: clear_facts` so that the role starts with no facts.

Create a task file tests/tasks/run_role_with_clear_facts.yml to do the tasks
to clear the facts and run the role.  Note that this means we don't need to
use `gather_facts` for the tests.

Some vars defined using `ansible_facts` have been changed to be defined with
`set_fact` instead.  This is because of the fact that `vars` are lazily
evaluated - the var might be referenced when the facts have been cleared, and
will issue an error like `ansible_facts["distribution"] is undefined`.  This is
typically done for blocks that have a `when` condition that uses `ansible_facts`
and the block has a role invocation using run_role_with_clear_facts.yml
These have been rewritten to define the `when` condition using `set_fact`.  This
is because the `when` condition is evaluated every time a task is invoked in the
block, and if the facts are cleared, this will raise an undefined variable error.

Signed-off-by: Rich Megginson <rmeggins@redhat.com>

## Summary by Sourcery

Run the trustee_attestation_client role in tests via a shared task file that clears facts before each role invocation.

Tests:
- Introduce a reusable tasks file that clears Ansible facts and then runs the trustee_attestation_client role for tests.
- Update existing test playbooks to use the new tasks file instead of direct role inclusion or gather_facts, ensuring the role runs without pre-gathered facts.

author: copilot
body:
Two flake8 errors were breaking CI: `F821 undefined name 'exc'` in several async lambda callbacks, and `E999 SyntaxError` from backslashes inside f-string expressions (Python < 3.12 restriction).

## `exc` captured in lambda default args
In Python 3, `except ... as exc` deletes `exc` from the local namespace at the end of the except block. Lambdas passed to `Clock.schedule_once` run after that deletion, causing a `NameError` at runtime and an `F821` from pyflakes. Fixed by binding `exc` as a default argument:

```python
# Before
except Exception as exc:
    Clock.schedule_once(lambda *_: setattr(self._info, "text", f"❌ {exc}"))

# After
except Exception as exc:
    Clock.schedule_once(lambda *_, e=exc: setattr(self._info, "text", f"❌ {e}"))
```

Affects 5 locations in `src/interface/kivy_local_ui.py` and 1 in `src/interface/kivy_remote_ui.py`.

## f-string backslash extraction
`'\n'` inside an f-string `{...}` expression is a syntax error on Python < 3.12. Fixed by hoisting the computation out:

```python
# Before
print(f"   ... и еще {len(changes.split('\n')) - 5} файлов")

# After
n_extra = len(changes.split('\n')) - 5
print(f"   ... и еще {n_extra} файлов")
```

Affects `validate_project.py` and `apps/argoss/validate_project.py` (line 202 in both).

📌 References
Issue: Closes https://app.clickup.com/t/869c8hupk
📝 Implementation
Problem:
We have been disabling users weekly because they weren't activating their 2FA. However, with the new release, we can now force 2FA activation. This means we no longer need to disable accounts so quickly; instead, we can target only those users who haven't set up 2FA within X months of their account creation.

Solution:
Added disableAfterMonths dataset setting.
Added the --filtered-by-month CLI flag to run-2fa-reporter. Although it doesn't accept a specific month value via CLI, it acts as a toggle to enable the filtering logic. This allows us to maintain the specific threshold in the Datastore for easy updates while giving us the flexibility to enable or disable filtering at the server level.

When enabled, only invalid users whose account was created >= [disableAfterMonths] ago are reported/disabled.
Throws an error if --filtered-by-month is used but is not configured in the datastore (invalid config).

body:
## Summary

This PR upgrades `google.golang.org/grpc` from v1.78.0 to v1.79.3 to fix a security vulnerability.

### Vulnerability Details

**Type:** Authorization Bypass via Improper Input Validation

The gRPC-Go server was too lenient in its routing logic, accepting requests where the `:path` pseudo-header omitted the mandatory leading slash (e.g., `Service/Method` instead of `/Service/Method`). While the server successfully routed these requests to the correct handler, authorization interceptors evaluated the raw, non-canonical path string, causing "deny" rules defined using canonical paths (starting with `/`) to fail to match the incoming request.

### Changes

- Updated `google.golang.org/grpc` from v1.78.0 to v1.79.3
- Updated related dependencies via `go mod tidy`

### Verification

- Code compiles successfully (agent and harness binaries built without errors in Docker)

### Files Modified

- `go.mod` - Updated grpc version
- `go.sum` - Updated checksums for dependencies

author: vatsanbalaji
body:
## What is the purpose of this PR

- This PR fixes the flaky test CaseServiceImplTest#testUpdateNotExistingCaseComment by enforcing deterministic XML field serialization order.

## Why The test fails

- The Test fails because JAXB serializes the fields of DeploymentDescriptorImpl and ObjectModel classes using Hashmap iteration order, which is nondeterministic. 
- When NonDex shuffles the Hashmap iteration order, XML elements are written in the wrong order, causing XML schema validation to fail with a MarshalException during test setup.

## How to Reproduce the test failure

Run the following commands

- `mvn clean install -DskipTests -pl jbpm-case-mgmt/jbpm-case-mgmt-impl -am`
- `mvn -pl jbpm-case-mgmt/jbpm-case-mgmt-impl edu.illinois:nondex-maven-plugin:2.1.1:nondex -Dtest=org.jbpm.casemgmt.impl.CaseServiceImplTest#testUpdateNotExistingCaseComment`

## Expected Results
 - The test should pass consistently with NonDex shuffling enabled across all seeds.
 
 ## Actual Results
 - The test fails with: javax.xml.bind.MarshalException - Invalid content was found starting with element because XML fields are serialized in wrong order.
 
 ## Description of fix
 - Added @XmlType(propOrder=...) annotation to DeploymentDescriptorImpl and ObjectModel to enforce deterministic XML field serialization order.
 - Changed Hashmap to LinkedHashMap in CaseFileInstanceMarshallingStrategy and AbstractServicesTest to preserve insertion order

body:
## Summary
- Problem: `pip install .` could build the native backends but still produce a wheel without any `core_*` modules, so fresh installs in CUDA-capable environments never exposed the `cuda` backend.
- Scope: fix wheel packaging for the native backend modules in `setup.py`; this does not change backend math or runtime selection logic.
- Outcome: built wheels now include the compiled native modules, and a fresh install exposes `gcc`, `openmp`, `mpi`, and `cuda` when the corresponding extensions are available.

This change makes the setuptools/CMake bridge copy native backend artifacts back into the package build directory before wheel assembly, instead of relying on them landing in the expected place automatically.

## Technical Details
- Approach: recursively collect compiled `core_*` extension artifacts from the CMake temp build tree and copy them into `build_lib/fpie` after `make`, so wheel packaging picks them up consistently across generators.
- Code pointers:
  - `setup.py`: copy native artifacts out of the nested CMake build tree before wheel assembly.
  - `setup.py`: stop relying on `package_data` for extension modules so dirty source-tree `.so` files from another platform do not leak into wheels.
- Notes: this addresses packaging/install visibility of native backends; it does not attempt to change the CUDA solver implementation itself.

## Test Plan
### Automated
- `python -m compileall setup.py`: passes
- On `dev2-0`, built a wheel from the patched tree and verified the wheel contains `core_cuda`, `core_gcc`, `core_mpi`, and `core_openmp`
- On `dev2-0`, installed the built wheel in a fresh venv and verified `fpie --check-backend` reports `['numpy', 'numba', 'taichi-cpu', 'taichi-gpu', 'gcc', 'openmp', 'cuda']`
### Suggested Manual
- `pip install .` on a CUDA-capable machine, then run `fpie --check-backend`
- Run one README example with `--backend cuda` to confirm the backend is both visible and runnable

💡 **What:** Extracted the sequential review processing into `processSingleReview()` and parallelized the workload in chunks of 5 using `Promise.all()`.

- **Sequential Baseline:** ~708ms
- **Optimized Chunks of 5:** ~148ms
A massive ~79% drop in total execution time. Using chunks prevents overwhelming external APIs or rate limits while still offering substantial concurrency.

body:
## Summary
Updated the Google Compute health check configuration for the trackrat service to use a readiness probe instead of a liveness probe and increased the unhealthy threshold tolerance.

## Key Changes
- Changed health check endpoint from `/health/live` to `/health/ready` to align with readiness probe semantics
- Increased `unhealthy_threshold` from 3 to 5 to reduce false positives and provide more tolerance for transient failures before marking an instance as unhealthy

## Implementation Details
These changes improve the stability of the health check by:
1. Using the readiness endpoint which better reflects whether the service is ready to accept traffic
2. Allowing more consecutive failed health checks (5 instead of 3) before removing an instance from the load balancer, reducing unnecessary instance churn during temporary service disruptions

author: obiloud
body:
### **Overview**
This PR transitions the backend architecture from a monolithic agent structure to a modular, multi-agent system. By implementing the **Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol**, the system now supports seamless handoffs between specialized agents, specifically separating the **Chat Gateway (Agent A)** from the **Synthesis Engine (Agent B)**.

---

### **Key Changes**

#### 🏗️ **Architectural Refactoring**
* **Modular Agent Structure:** Relocated agent-specific logic to `backend/agent_a_chat` and `backend/agent_b_synth`.
* **Shared Utilities:** Created a `backend/shared` directory to house common logic and models, improving maintainability.
* **A2A Server Integration:** Fully implemented Agent B as an A2A-compliant server with defined agent cards and a managed execution lifecycle (start/work/complete/cancel).

#### 💾 **State & Workflow Management**
* **Unified State Model:** Standardized the shared state as `ChatState` (formerly `ConversationState`) to ensure consistency across the agent chain.
* **Orchestration Logic:** Added `trigger_synth` fields to handle the handoff trigger between agents.
* **LangGraph Enhancements:** Enabled persistence across sessions by integrating checkpointer and store support within LangGraph workflows.

#### ⚙️ **DevOps & Environment**
* **Improved Configuration:** Transitioned from hardcoded values to standardized environment variables (`POSTGRES_CONNECTION_STRING` and `HF_TOKEN`).
* **Dependency Updates:** Updated `a2a-sdk` to include `http-server` extras for HTTP endpoint serving.
* **Docker Optimization:** Updated Dockerfiles to reflect the new directory hierarchy and ensure consistent builds.

---

### **Impact**
* Enables scalable agent orchestration.
* Improves debugging through structured, persistent state.
* Provides a standardized foundation for adding future specialized agents to the chain.

`docker compose up -d` re-evaluates `depends_on` healthcheck even when images are pre-built. VaultCenter in `setup` state doesn't pass the healthcheck (`curl -fsk .../health` returns non-zero for `{"status":"setup"}`), causing localvault/veil to fail with "dependency failed to start: unhealthy".

Use `--no-deps` for all service starts. VaultCenter is confirmed healthy via manual polling before starting dependents.

author: copilot
body:
On fresh installs, `pv_today` history is often < 24 hours old (`age.days == 0`), producing an empty `mdata` dict that gets passed to `clean_incrementing_reverse()`, which immediately crashes on `max(data)`.

## Change

Added an early-return guard in `utils.py`:

```python
def clean_incrementing_reverse(data, max_increment=0):
    new_data = {}
    if not data:
        return new_data  # nothing to clean
    length = max(data) + 1
```

Returning `{}` is semantically correct — the caller (`minute_data`) already handles empty `mdata` gracefully, and there is nothing to smooth when no data exists.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> 
> ----
> 
> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>`clean_incrementing_reverse` crashes with `ValueError: max() arg is empty`  when history < 24 hours</issue_title>
> <issue_description>## Description
> 
> `clean_incrementing_reverse()` in `utils.py` crashes with `ValueError: max() arg is an empty sequence` when called with an empty dict. This happens during the SolarAPI / PV calibration flow on a fresh install where pv_today history is less than 24 hours old.
> 
> ## Stack trace
> 
> ```
> File "/config/solcast.py", line 967, in fetch_pv_forecast
>     pv_forecast_minute, pv_forecast_minute10, pv_forecast_data = self.pv_calibration(...)
> File "/config/solcast.py", line 657, in pv_calibration
>     pv_today_hist = self.base.minute_data_import_export(days, self.now_utc, "pv_today", required_unit="kWh", pad=False)
> File "/config/fetch.py", line 578, in minute_data_import_export
>     import_today, _ = minute_data(...)
> File "/config/utils.py", line 624, in minute_data
>     mdata = clean_incrementing_reverse(mdata, max_increment)
> ValueError: max() arg is an empty sequence
> ```
> 
> ## Root cause
> 
> In `minute_data_import_export()`, when `pad=False` is passed (as `pv_calibration` does), the function uses `age.days` instead of the requested `max_days_previous`:
> 
> ```python
> age = now_utc - last_updated_time
> age_days = min(age_days, age.days)
> ```
> 
> If the oldest history entry is less than 24 hours old, `age.days == 0`. This is passed to `minute_data()` which computes `minute_min = 0` and `minute_max = 0`, so no history entries fall within bounds and `mdata` remains `{}`.
> 
> `mdata` is then passed to `clean_incrementing_reverse()`, which immediately calls `max(data)` on the empty dict:
> 
> ```python
> def clean_incrementing_reverse(data, max_increment=0):
>     new_data = {}
>     length = max(data) + 1  # <-- crashes here when data is {}
> ```
> 
> ## Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Fresh Predbat install with Solcast enabled
> 2. pv_today sensor (e.g. `sensor.foxess_solar_energy_today`) has less than 24 hours of history
> 3. Predbat runs its first cycle with SolarAPI → crash every cycle until history crosses 24h
> 
> ## Suggested fix
> 
> Add an empty-data guard at the top of `clean_incrementing_reverse()`:
> 
> ```python
> def clean_incrementing_reverse(data, max_increment=0):
>     new_data = {}
>     if not data:
>         return new_data
>     length = max(data) + 1
> ```
> 
> ## Workaround applied
> 
> I patched `utils.py` directly on the addon container by adding an empty-data guard to `clean_incrementing_reverse()`:
> 
> ```python
> def clean_incrementing_reverse(data, max_increment=0):
>     new_data = {}
>     if not data:
>         return new_data  # <-- added guard
>     length = max(data) + 1
> ```
> 
> This works because:
> 
> - The function is only called from `minute_data()` when `clean_increment=True` and data is backwards (historical). When `mdata` is empty, there is nothing to clean — returning an empty dict is the correct no-op behaviour.
> - The caller (`minute_data`) already handles empty `mdata` gracefully downstream — it simply means no historical data was available for that time window.
> - After applying this patch and restarting Predbat, the SolarAPI crash stopped immediately. Predbat completed its cycle successfully with status "Demand" and no errors.
> 
> **Note:** This patch will be overwritten on the next Predbat addon update since the addon replaces all source files. However, the crash condition is only triggered during the first ~24 hours after a fresh install (while `age.days == 0`), so it is unlikely to recur after an update on an established system.
> 
> ## Environment
> 
> - Predbat v8.34.5 (standalone addon)
> - Inverter: FoxESS KH10-AUX (foxess_modbus v1.13.6)
> - Solcast: BJReplay/ha-solcast-solar v4.5.1
> - Home Assistant 2026.3.2
> </issue_description>

author: anzzyspeaksgit
body:
## Problem
When calling `AliasGetReq` without specifying `Indices` (or providing an empty `Indices` array/slice), the resulting API path incorrectly contains a double slash.
For example, it might produce `//_alias/test-alias` instead of `/_alias/test-alias`. This double slash causes issues for proxies or when interacting with some clusters, such as Aiven where this causes failures (see #617).

## Solution
I modified the `GetRequest` function in `opensearchapi/api_indices-alias.go` to conditionally append the initial `/` and `indices` string only if `indices` is not empty. If `indices` is empty, it appends only `/_alias/` and the aliases name(s), ensuring the URL path is valid (e.g. `/_alias/test-alias`).

## Testing
- Verified via `make test` that all existing tests pass correctly.

Closes #617

author: copilot
body:
The tile/zone/furniture rendering pipeline was fully defined but never connected — `render.ts` made no calls to `drawTileLayer`, zone overlays, or furniture drawing, so the map displayed as a plain dark background with only players visible.

## render.ts — wire the rendering pipeline

Draw order now follows the intended z-ordering:

```
background → dot-grid → vignette
  → floor tiles (z < 1)
  → zone colour overlays
  → wall tiles (z >= 1)
  → furniture
  → debug colliders → players → particles → HUD
```

Added `drawFurniture()` to handle both `rect` and `circle` shapes, including `tileSprite` rendering (scales the tile to fill the furniture rect) with a solid-colour fallback while sheets are loading.

## map.ts — richer floor patterns (STATIC_GAME_MAP)

- **Room border rings** — 1-tile perimeter of each zone uses the darker variant of that zone's tile palette, creating a subtle inset frame
- **Lounge centre rug** — 7×9 tile beige/tan accent area on the wood floor, with a tan border ring (`_RUG_C1/C2`, `_RUG_R1/R2`)
- **Meeting carpet** — flat beige underlay beneath the conference table area (`_CARPET_*`)
- **Reception mat** — 4×2 darker office tile at the OW corridor doorway (`_MAT_*`)

All special-feature bounds are extracted as named constants derived from the existing layout constants (`_DH_L1`, `_WC1`, etc.) rather than raw magic numbers.

## room-generator.ts — same improvements for the active GAME_MAP

`GAME_MAP = generateGameMap(0)` is the live path, so floor improvements needed to land here too.

- `fillFloorBorder()` — paints a 1-tile perimeter using `r + 1` to flip row parity, guaranteeing the border always picks the alternate shade of the same theme without a separate dark-theme lookup
- `fillFloorRect()` — flat theme fill for rugs and carpets
- `fillFloorBorder` called for all 6 rooms; Lounge rug and Meeting carpet added for the matching room purposes

Adds a `PlayerSelectModal` component that lets users select previously saved players (preserving their UUIDs) instead of retyping names each round. Wired into the Start Round flow. ## Component (`PlayerSelectModal`) - **Portal** rendered via a self-managed container `
` (avoids RTL/cleanup conflicts with `document.body`) - **Props:** `isOpen`, `players`, `preselectedIds`, `onConfirm(selectedIds[])`, `onClose`, `allowAddNew`, `maxSelectable` - **Search:** 200 ms debounced filter input with clear button - **List:** scrollable (`max-height: 60vh`), checkbox per row with truncated UUID metadata and optional avatar - **Footer:** "Cancel" / "Confirm (N)" — disabled at 0 selected; `onConfirm` returns IDs in selection order (pre-selected IDs keep their original order; newly checked IDs are appended in click order) - **`allowAddNew`:** inline "+ Add player" form — saves to IndexedDB, auto-selects the new entry (skips auto-select if already at `maxSelectable`) - **`maxSelectable`:** enforces a selection cap — unselected checkboxes are disabled when the limit is reached; a `X/max` counter badge in the header (e.g. `2/6`) turns the accent colour at the limit - **`preselectedIds` safety:** on open, unknown/stale IDs are intersected against available players so the selection count and Confirm state always reflect reality - **Keyboard:** Esc cancels, Tab/Shift-Tab focus trap, Arrow Up/Down navigates checkboxes, Enter confirms - **A11y:** `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby`, visually-hidden `aria-live` region for selection count - State resets on each open transition; closing without confirming discards changes ## StartRound integration - Shows **"Select from existing players"** when DB players exist **or** when players have been manually typed on the page - On open: persists any manually-typed players to IndexedDB (via `Promise.all`) and re-fetches the player list, ensuring those players appear in the modal with their checkboxes correctly pre-checked - On confirm: re-fetches DB (captures any in-modal additions), maps IDs → `Player` objects via an id→player `Map` (preserves modal selection order, O(n) lookup) - Passes `maxSelectable={MAX_PLAYERS_PER_ROUND}` so the modal enforces the 6-player cap directly in the UI - Extracted the magic `6` limit into a named constant `MAX_PLAYERS_PER_ROUND` - Selected players are displayed as a **numbered list** on the Start Round screen ## Tests 46 interaction tests cover: open/close, backdrop/Esc, search+debounce, select/deselect, confirm ordering, keyboard navigation, add-new flow, state reset on re-open, counter display, disabled checkboxes at max, re-enable after deselect, and unknown `preselectedIds` being safely ignored. ```tsx p.id)} onConfirm={handleModalConfirm} onClose={() => setModalOpen(false)} allowAddNew maxSelectable={MAX_PLAYERS_PER_ROUND} /> ``` ## Note Virtualization (`react-window`) for >200 players was not added — unnecessary new dependency for a disc-golf app where that scale is unrealistic.

The navigation sidebar had hardcoded menu items with no mechanism to show/hide them based on application configuration. This adds a settings-driven visibility layer backed by a new `AppSetting` entity and API.

## Backend
- **`Erp.Domain/Models/AppSetting.cs`** — new `AppSetting` model (`Id`, `SysKey`, `SysValue`, `Remarks`)
- **`ErpDbContext`** — added `AppSetting` DbSet
- **`AppSettingsController`** — `GET /api/AppSettings` and `GET /api/AppSettings/{key}`

## Frontend
- **`AppSettingsService`** — fetches settings on load; exposes `isMenuItemVisible(settingKey)` with fail-open default (item shown if setting is missing or API unavailable)
- **`MenuItem` interface** — added optional `settingKey` property
- **`NavigationComponent`** — assigns setting keys to each top-level item; `menuItems` is now a `computed()` signal filtered through the settings service

```typescript
menuItems = computed(() =>
  this.allMenuItems().filter(item =>
    !item.settingKey || this.appSettingsService.isMenuItemVisible(item.settingKey)
  )
);
```

Supported setting keys: `SHOW_JOBORDERS`, `SHOW_MASTERFILES`, `SHOW_REFERENCES`, `SHOW_AGENTFORM`.

## Tests

## Summary
Complete the domain migration from `skatehubba.xyz` to `skatehubba.com` by implementing 301 redirects, pinning the Firebase auth domain, and documenting all required manual infrastructure steps.

## Key Changes

- **Vercel redirects:** Added permanent 301 redirects in `vercel.json` for `skatehubba.xyz`, `www.skatehubba.xyz`, and `www.skatehubba.com` → `skatehubba.com` to preserve SEO equity and handle legacy domain traffic
- **Firebase auth domain pinning:** Modified `src/firebase.ts` to pin `authDomain` to `skatehubba.com` in production builds, preventing OAuth redirect mismatches if users reach the app via the old domain before the redirect fires
- **Documentation:** Added comprehensive deployment guide in `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` with a complete checklist of completed code changes and manual infrastructure steps (Vercel, DNS, Firebase Auth, Google Cloud Console)
- **Architecture notes:** Updated `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` to document the 301 redirect strategy as part of the deployment architecture

## Implementation Details

The Firebase auth domain pinning uses `VITE_APP_URL` environment variable to detect production builds and only applies the override when the canonical URL is set, allowing development and preview deployments to use their respective auth domains.

All hardcoded URLs in static files (`index.html`, `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt`) already reference `.com`, and `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` is applied to non-canonical hosts via existing Vercel headers configuration.

author: copilot
body:
Users have no way to download and run the Pong game on Windows without a pre-installed JRE. This adds a GitHub Actions release pipeline that produces a bundled Windows installer on every `v*` tag.

## New workflow: `.github/workflows/release.yml`

- **Trigger:** `push` on `v*` tags (e.g. `v1.0.0`)
- **Runner:** `windows-latest`, JDK 25 Temurin (matches project toolchain)
- **Build:** `./gradlew clean build` (compile + tests + JAR in one pass)
- **Packaging via `jpackage`** — bundles a JRE so no Java install is required:
  - **MSI** (preferred) — installs with Start Menu shortcut, uninstallable via Add/Remove Programs
  - **EXE** fallback — if WiX MSI generation fails
  - **app-image ZIP** last resort — extract-and-run folder
- **Artifact naming:** `PongApp-v1.0.0-windows.{msi,exe,zip}` uploaded directly to the GitHub Release for the triggering tag via `softprops/action-gh-release@v2`

**Version normalization:** tag `v1.0` is padded to `1.0.0` to satisfy the Windows MSI `x.y.z` version format requirement.

```yaml
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'
```

body:
## Summary

- Removes `#` comment lines from inside `claude_args` in all three Claude workflows (`claude-code-review.yml`, `claude-test-review.yml`, `claude.yml`)
- `shell-quote` (used by `claude-code-action` to parse `claude_args`) treats `#` as a comment character, causing all flags that appear after any comment line to be **silently dropped** — meaning `--max-turns`, `--allowedTools`, and `--model` were all being ignored
- Restores `--model ${{ inputs.model }}` as the intended mechanism for model selection per the action's documentation
- Documents the `#` comment restriction in `CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOWS.md`

## Root Cause

This is [upstream issue anthropics/claude-code-action#802](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/issues/802). The `shell-quote` library parses the `claude_args` multiline string and treats `#` as a shell comment, dropping everything after it on a line — including all subsequent flag lines.

## Test Plan

- [ ] Trigger a test PR in a consuming repo (e.g. `liquibase-license-generator`) referencing this branch
- [ ] Confirm run logs show `"model": "claude-haiku-4-5"` in the SDK init message
- [ ] Confirm `total_cost_usd` reflects Haiku pricing (~75% lower than Sonnet)
- [ ] Confirm `--max-turns` and `--allowedTools` restrictions are honored

author: copilot
body:
Bootstrap a Flask web app that generates platform-tailored social media posts via the Groq API (`openai/gpt-oss-120b`) with real-time streaming output.

## Backend (`app.py`)
- `/generate` endpoint accepts platform, tone, free-text, and optional file upload; builds a platform+tone-aware prompt and streams the Groq API response back as `text/plain`
- Text extraction for PDF (`PyPDF2`), DOCX (`python-docx`), and TXT uploads
- API key read from `GROQ_API_KEY` env var; debug mode gated behind `FLASK_DEBUG` env var (never hardcoded)
- File uploads validated by extension allowlist and capped at 10 MB (`secure_filename` applied)

## Frontend (`templates/`, `static/`)
- Three-step UI: platform picker (Twitter/X, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, Threads) → tone picker (Professional / Funny / LOL) → content (textarea + drag-and-drop file upload)
- Streams response word-by-word into the output card using `ReadableStream`; copy-to-clipboard and regenerate actions

## Prompt design
Platform guidelines (character limits, hashtag conventions) and tone guidelines are injected per-selection:

```python
PLATFORM_GUIDELINES = {
    "twitter": "Twitter/X (max 280 characters, use hashtags, short and punchy)",
    "linkedin": "LinkedIn (professional network, paragraph format, up to 3000 characters)",
    ...
}
TONE_GUIDELINES = {
    "professional": "professional, formal, and authoritative tone...",
    "lol": "extremely hilarious, over-the-top comedic tone with memes references...",
    ...
}
```

## Config
- `requirements.txt`: `flask`, `requests`, `python-dotenv`, `PyPDF2`, `python-docx`
- `.env.example` documents required env vars; `.gitignore` excludes `.env` and build artifacts
