author: albertkellner
body:
## Motivos da alteração

O usuário solicitou que, ao verificar se os logs seguem o padrão "storytelling flow" (SNP-001), os logs disparados para cada requisição sejam apresentados explicitamente na resposta. Atualmente, a regra de validação de endpoint (`endpoint-validation.md`) exige status code, endpoint completo e JSON da resposta — mas não exige a apresentação dos logs de storytelling. Isso torna a verificação do padrão implícita e invisível para o usuário.

## Plano de execução

1. Adicionar Passo 3.1 em `endpoint-validation.md` para captura de logs imediatamente após cada chamada HTTP
2. Adicionar item 4 ao Passo 5 (relatório) exigindo logs de storytelling com verificação visual do padrão SNP-001
3. Refinar passo 7 do pipeline em `CLAUDE.md` para referenciar a obrigação per-endpoint da rule
4. Executar checklist REVIEW.md para validar consistência

## O que foi realizado

### `.claude/rules/endpoint-validation.md`
- **Passo 3.1 (novo)**: Captura obrigatória de logs do container imediatamente após cada chamada HTTP, com filtro por CorrelationId ou proximidade temporal
- **Passo 5, item 4 (novo)**: Logs de storytelling da requisição como item obrigatório no relatório de validação, com critérios de verificação visual: prefixo `[Classe][Método]`, logs de entrada/saída, sequência narrativa coerente
- **Histórico de Mudanças**: Entrada adicionada para 2026-03-20

### `CLAUDE.md`
- **Pipeline Passo 7**: Refinado para referenciar a obrigação per-endpoint de `endpoint-validation.md` e delegar para `docker logs` apenas quando o passo 6 não for aplicável

### Revisão REVIEW.md
- Checklists 1 (localização), 2 (duplicação), 3 (separação), 5 (consistência) executados — todos passaram

author: seanmcguire12
body: # why - so that routes always return the same result shape, which can contain one, many, or no selectors depending on a user specified `returnSelector` param # what changed - added an optional `returnSelector` param to `/click`, `/hover`, and `/dragAndDrop` - each of these routes will ALWAYS have a `selector` object in their responses, but if `returnSelector` is not truthy, then the `selector` object will be empty - `/dragAndDrop` response will contain a `startSelector` and `endSelector` - added `ResultSelectorSchema` which can carry any combination of `xpath`, `css`, `text`, and `coordinates` (nested `{ x, y }`) - replaced `PageXPathResultSchema` with dedicated `PageClickResultSchema` and `PageHoverResultSchema`, each wrapping a `ResultSelectorSchema` - replaced `PageDragAndDropResultSchema` fields (`fromXpath`/`toXpath`) with `startSelector/endSelector` using `ResultSelectorSchema` - removed `PageXPathResultSchema` (no longer used by any route) - removed dead `normalizeXPath` helper from `shared.ts` --- ## Summary by cubic Standardized v4 page action responses to always return selector objects, with an optional returnSelector flag to control selector data. Updates click, hover, dragAndDrop, and scroll stubs/schemas for a consistent result shape, aligning with Linear STG-1638. - New Features - Added returnSelector?: boolean to /click, /hover, and /dragAndDrop. - click/hover now return selector; dragAndDrop returns startSelector and endSelector. These are empty unless returnSelector is true. - Introduced ResultSelectorSchema supporting xpath, css, text, and coordinates. - Migration - Replace PageXPathResultSchema with PageClickResultSchema and PageHoverResultSchema. - For dragAndDrop, migrate from fromXpath/toXpath to startSelector/endSelector. - Scroll now returns PageScrollResultSchema with { x, y } instead of an xpath result. - Removed PageXPathResultSchema and the normalizeXPath helper; update imports. Written for commit cfc858b339b328e8b60bd2867abd0521cae21f7c. Summary will update on new commits. Review in cubic

author: hudua
body:
This pull request updates documentation and infrastructure templates to reflect the latest supported AI models and deployment practices for Azure Foundry and Azure Machine Learning (AML), with an emphasis on Canadian data residency and managed compute deployment options. It also introduces minor improvements to deployment configuration and clarity in the Bicep infrastructure code.

**Documentation updates:**

* Updated the list of AI Foundry models that support in-transit data processing within Canada, including new models like `gpt-4.1-mini`, `gpt-5-mini`, `gpt-5`, and `gpt-5.1`, and clarified model availability and deployment options.
* Added guidance on deploying pre-trained Foundry large language models with managed compute and emphasized the use of private endpoints for security.

**Infrastructure and configuration improvements:**

* Added an `amlType` variable to `aml-workspace.bicep` to allow switching the Azure ML workspace kind between `'Default'` and `'hub'`, supporting both standard and Foundry LLM managed compute deployments. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-24980b6067128297da817569790021ec7ef9524c56b7c3fd1700859f49aff30fR47-R48) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-24980b6067128297da817569790021ec7ef9524c56b7c3fd1700859f49aff30fL74-R76)
* Removed the `egress_public_network_access: disabled` setting from `deployment-generic.yml` and `deployment-vllm.yml` to align with updated deployment requirements or defaults.
